w: At 10-05 a.m. Swamishri arrived at Tajpur village to perform the ground-breaking ceremony for a new mandir. While going to the site Swamishri offered his respect to Yagneshwar Mahadev.

In the assembly Swamishri talked about the glory of Tajpur, "The association with this village started when the mandir in Sarangpur was being built. Shastriji Maharaj used to come here a lot. And the devotees of this village had offered their tremendous services in the construction of the mandir in Sarangpur. And Shastri Maharaj had a special bond with this village. The devotees, though of ordinary means, participated in festivals held at the mandir in Sarangpur.

"Shastriji Maharaj used to travel to these small villages. The homes were small with little arrangements. But before the love and affection of the devotees there was no need for facilities. It was because of the love of Shabri that Lord Ram accepted berries from her...

"This village was also blessed by Yogiji Maharaj. Swami also used to come here often... The village has developed a lot since then. There was a small mandir here and now a bigger mandir will be built. Since the devotees are enthusiastic the new mandir will take shape within no time."
Swamishri performed the ground-breaking ceremony at the auspicious time of 12.05 p.m. 1000 devotees and well-wishers had attended the occasion.
After lunch Swamishri returned to Sarangpur at 1.40 p.m.

After his evening dinner Swamishri met a devotee called Bhayabhai. Bhayabhai humbly expressed his wish to Swamishri, "Bapa, I want to please you." Swamishri replied, "Do bhajan and inspire Satsang in others."
Swamishri offered pujan of bricks to be placed in the foundation of a mandir in the village of Khijalpur, Umreth.
In the evening assembly, children presented an agenda of speeches, monoacting, drama ('Swadhyayan Ma Pramadah') and dance. Finally Swamishri blessed the assembly.

Before his morning puja, Swamishri went to Yagnapurush Smruti Mandir for darshan. Then he went to Yagnapurush Gaushala to inaugurate the new offices, mobile veterinary dispensary and the animal treatment center. After puja, Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha rituals of pujan and arti for the murtis to be installed at the new hari mandir in Chandrasar (dist: Surendranagar).

In the evening assembly a drama ‘Padvuj Nathi’, depicting the dangers of fault-finding, was effectively performed in the presence of Swamishri. In his blessings Swamishri said, “Firstly, we must understand why we come to Satsang – to rid ourselves of our base nature and personal failings. One must always look at oneself first. When you feel that you are pure and spotless then you will see faults in others. But when you think that you want to become brahmarup then you should see what faults you have and make efforts to get rid of them.”

The festivals of Bhagatji Maharaj’s birthday and Fuldol were celebrated in the evening from 5.15 p.m to 8.30 p.m. Swamishri blessed and sprayed more than 60,000 devotees with sanctified coloured water. (Details in April 2009 issue).

A seeker from Surat came for darshan. Until now he had spent 50 lakh rupees on his addictions. Today he had come, after Swamishri's blessings, to vow to give up all his addictions. Swamishri was pleased.
Many people in society believe that once Pramukh Swami Maharaj's hand is placed on your head, you are freed from the grip of addiction.

Nilkanthseva Swami, training at the sadhu training centre, said to Swamishri, "Our class held a discussion on why you should receive the Nobel Peace Prize. We examined in detail why you should get it. Today the whole world is discussing how to stop terrorism. Most people's response is that terrorists must be dealt with harshly. But the response you gave when Akshardham was attacked by terrorists was unique in the world, and everyone felt it was worth following. For this one act alone you should receive the Nobel Peace Prize."

All the sadhus sitting here joined in with Nilkanthseva Swami. Swamishri too was listening to everyone. One sadhu said, "You should get the Nobel Peace Prize. Even if you do not wish for it, you could refuse it. That would make an even greater impression on people! Satsang would grow endlessly."

Swamishri said, "Even to have such a thought, that everyone should give the Nobel Prize, is wrong. The thought should not come at all. Do not even keep the wish that others do such things. What is there beyond receiving the blessings of Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj? Even the thought that others should do this is a flaw. Even having such a wish is a flaw. We do not go to anyone to recommend it or say anything, but the wish has come into the mind! Why should such a wish come at all?"
Madhurvadan Swami said, "That is your feeling, but surely we must keep the wish that your greatness grows?"
Swamishri said, "Having met Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj, everything is included. Maharaj said, and Jogi Bapa says too, that there is no title higher than sadhu. What is greater than that?"
The sadhus kept arguing in turn. Bhadresh Swami too said, "That you do not wish for it is your greatness, but the disciples may try, can't they?"
Swamishri said, "There is no need to even have such a wish."
The sadhus said, "In the end we too, thinking this way, sang a line. We will sing it now." Saying this,
'Those who leave behind worldly pleasures,
what can we ever offer them?
There is nothing in the world for them,
forever carefree in Hari's colour.'
Everyone sang this verse. Swamishri only smiled.

Nilkanthseva Swami said, "You once said that you received Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj, the prize of prizes beyond the Nobel Prize. In the same way, what is the Nobel Prize to us? We have received you, the prize of our peace prizes."
Swamishri said, "Yes, that I met you and you met us, that itself is the Nobel Prize."
A son had been born to the daughter of Shri Tejendra Khanna, Lieutenant Governor of Delhi. He had been named 'Kedar'. Shri Khanna wished to receive Swamishri's blessings for him.
Blessing them on the phone, Swamishri said, "A child has been born in your daughter's home. My blessings are that he receives good values and becomes cultured, stays healthy and is happy."
Shri Khanna said, "That I have received your blessings is the greatest thing. I am very grateful to you."
